map.default_provider_name: Electricity production ; Electricity mix ; China (geo CN, year 2019, source 能源统计年鉴2020)
map.why: The hint flow 'Electricity' (890a70b7) is correct and well connected (34 producers, 945 consumers); it is the flow every grid-mix dataset in TianGong outputs. TianGong has no Korean grid at all (searches for Korea, KR, 电力, grid, power returned only Chinese datasets), so a geographic proxy is unavoidable. The China national mix 2019 is the neutral default: geo CN, recent year, a documented statistical source, reference output exactly 3.6 MJ (= 1 kWh), and its only linked input ('electricity for thermal power', 2.505 MJ per 3.6 MJ) resolves by the repo's geo rule to 'Electricity production ; Thermal power ; China' (aef876a0), a gate-to-gate dataset with real elementary flows (CO2 fossil 0.834 kg, SO2 1.4e-4 kg, NOx 2.3e-4 kg per kWh of thermal output). Implied grid intensity is 0.696 × 0.834 = 0.58 kg CO2/kWh, consistent with China's official 2019 grid factor. What it misrepresents: Korea's grid around 2009-2011 was roughly 40 % coal, 31 % nuclear, 22 % gas, 3 % oil, with a published factor of about 0.46-0.50 kg CO2/kWh, so the CN mix overstates CO2 by roughly 15-25 % and overstates SO2/NOx more (coal-heavy thermal share, no gas split). The alternatives are chosen to make the sensitivity exercise meaningful: Guangdong (a976ee9d: 68 % thermal, 22 % nuclear, ~0.48 kg CO2/kWh) is the structurally closest Chinese proxy to the Korean 2011 mix and could be argued as a better default; Zhejiang (ed589f98: 71 % thermal, 18 % nuclear, ~0.47) and Fujian (2f580165: 55 % thermal, 24 % nuclear, ~0.43) are similar nuclear-plus-thermal coastal grids; Sichuan (30558cec: 85 % hydro, ~0.11) and Inner Mongolia (1dbf3ef8: 84 % thermal with the dirtiest thermal process, ~0.91) bracket the full range. All 31 provincial mixes output the same flow with ref amount 3.6 MJ, so any of them is a drop-in provider. Because electricity is the dominant input in both systems (operation stage = 60 % of SVE and 56 % of biopile normalised impact in the paper), this provider choice is the single most influential background decision in the case and should be the headline sensitivity.
map.data_quality_notes: (1) Three of the 34 'producers' of flow Electricity are mis-tagged fragments from a biomass-jet-fuel thesis (0092e030, 15df6697, 42b76a15): their reference exchange is an INPUT of Electricity (they consume their own reference flow), year is None, and they must never be used as providers; the repo resolver would skip them anyway (year None loses to 2019) but they pollute `producers` listings. (2) Every 'Electricity mix' process has inputs summing to exactly 3.6 MJ per 3.6 MJ output: no transmission and distribution losses (~5-6 % in both China and Korea) and no plant own-use are modelled, so delivered electricity is slightly under-burdened. (3) In the mix, the hydro, nuclear, wind and solar inputs have zero producers and become cut-offs; their direct emissions are near zero so the omission mainly drops infrastructure burdens, but the tool will list ~30 % of the national mix (and up to 88 % for Sichuan/Yunnan/Qinghai) as unlinked MJ. (4) 'Thermal power ; China' is explicitly direct-combustion only ('does not consider upstream raw material extraction'); its dominant inputs raw coal (0.394 kg/kWh) and washed coal have no producers, so coal mining and transport (methane, mining energy) are cut off; natural gas (20 producers) and coke (45 producers) will be linked by the resolver, bringing in some unintended upstream. Particulates are tagged as a Waste flow, not an elementary flow, so PM is not characterised; no mercury or other heavy metals. (5) The snapshot's Acidification, EF-particulate, eutrophication and ozone methods list the same (SO2, out) and (NOx, out) keys many times with different values (regionalised rows sharing one flow uuid, e.g. SO2 from 0.012 to 4.524 mol H+/kg); reference/lca_matrix.py builds Q with a dict comprehension so the last row silently wins. Since SO2/NOx from the electricity provider drive the acidification result, this should be made deterministic (pick the generic factor) before quoting acidification numbers. (6) The LCIA flow coverage for the electricity chain is otherwise fine: CO2 fossil is characterised at 1.0 in both Climate change methods. (7) Flow name has leading/trailing spaces in ' Electricity for thermal power ' (b4eb7d84) — cosmetic, but exact-name searches miss it.

map.default_provider_name: Carbonization, activation ; Coal activated carbon ; Raw material coal ; Physical activation process ; All sizes; NESPS2 (CN, 2019)
map.why: Technology match: the paper's GAC LCI (Bayer et al. 2005) is hard-coal GAC made by steam (physical) activation, and vapour-phase GAC for VOC off-gas is typically coal- or coconut-based physically activated carbon; c090f0c3 is the CN-2019 coal / physical-activation dataset, geo CN and recent, with real elementary flows (per t AC: SO2 2.78 kg, NOx 3.52 kg, PM 0.94 kg). TianGong splits the coal route into four unit operations that all have ref output 1000 kg AC (crushing/sieving b74addfe, carbonization/activation c090f0c3, transport/storage d69afaef, flushing 6ecb514c); the matrix can link only one, but the other three carry almost nothing (0.0023 kg PM, no elementary flows, 0.0064 kg COD per t), so choosing c090f0c3 alone reproduces >99% of what TianGong has for coal AC and does not consume its own reference flow. What it misrepresents: like every NESPS2 dataset it has NO inputs at all (no coal feedstock, steam, electricity or gas), so the energy-intensive manufacture that makes GAC 36% of SVE's normalised impact in the paper is absent and the tool will show GWP ~0 for GAC against roughly 100-200 t CO2 implied by the paper (literature cradle-to-gate GWP of coal-based virgin GAC is of order 8-11 kg CO2-eq/kg, e.g. Bayer et al. 2005 and ecoinvent 'activated carbon, granular from hard coal' - cited from memory, verify before quoting). Suggested handling for the teaching exercise: keep c090f0c3 as the linked provider for direct process emissions and present the missing manufacture energy as a documented, optional add-on (~10 kg CO2-eq/kg GAC, i.e. ~180 t for SVE and ~14 t for biopile) in the discussion of why the TianGong result diverges from Table 5. Alternatives: a83ed2c4 (fruit-shell, physical activation, single gate-to-gate process, CN 2019) is the nearest biomass analogue (coconut-shell GAC is also used for vapour adsorption) and the natural sensitivity case; 8e839591 (NO 2011, Sparrevik et al., black box) is the only dataset with any input linked (electricity 1.36 MJ/kg) but its coal 1.89 kg/kg and road transport 0.905 kg/kg are cut-offs and it has no elementary flows, so it is not better; 4b8ba0f1 (wood chips, chemical activation) is a different product (chemical activation is mainly for powdered AC) and emits 254 kg PM/t, which would dominate the PM category for no good reason.
map.data_quality_notes: (1) All six NESPS2 producers are direct-emission coefficient datasets (第二次全国污染源普查产排污核算系数手册): zero product or energy inputs, only air/water pollutant outputs, so cradle-to-gate energy, CO2 and feedstock are entirely missing. (2) Each NESPS2 process carries repeated exchange rows for the same elementary flow: c090f0c3 has two rows each for PM, SO2, NOx and Exhaust gas; a83ed2c4 has three identical SO2 rows (0.47 kg) and five PM rows; 4b8ba0f1 has five PM rows summing to 253.7 kg/t. These look like several census coefficient rows (sub-technologies or control levels) loaded side by side; the matrix sums them, so c090f0c3's emissions are probably ~2x a single-technology value. (3) Every NESPS2 producer also emits a non-reference product output 'Exhaust gas' (14d56ab9, m3, ~114,000 m3/t for c090f0c3) and the biomass/flushing ones a 'Waste water' flow 72721c4e that has no type or unit in the snapshot; per the matrix conventions these are ignored for A and show up as unlinked outputs, harmless but noisy. (4) The coal route is four fragments with identical ref output (1000 kg AC); linking one loses the others, but the loss is negligible as quantified above. (5) 8e839591 (NO 2011): ref output 47,600,000 kg; per kg AC inputs coal 1.890 kg (flow 0e894e31, 0 producers), electricity 1.359 MJ (34 producers), 'Road Transport' 0.905 kg (flow 9462b645, 0 producers, mass unit for a transport service is a unit mismatch); no elementary flows of its own. (6) Flows 'Coal-based powdered activated carbon' (0212cd93) and 'Biochar based powdered activated carbon' (8273217c) exist but have 0 producers; 'Granular active carbon unit' (87f1d444) is an infrastructure item in Item(s), wrong scope. (7) The two KR-2011 curated processes (2f2acd1d SVE 18,000 kg; 517a7de8 biopile 1,368 kg) confirm the hint flow and amounts; 2f2acd1d also emits 18,000 kg 'Waste (solid)' for spent GAC, which the foreground here does not model.

convert.note: kg mortar -> kg Portland cement. The item is the well-annulus seal above the bentonite plug (bentonite 211 kg is a separate line). Sensitivity: if the paper's 'mortar' is in fact neat cement grout (ASTM D5092: 94 lb cement + ~6.5 gal water, w/c ~0.58) the cement fraction is ~0.63, i.e. 2.5x higher; if 2,291 kg is wet-mixed mortar mass, ~0.20.

Every check reproduces: the flow is a kg Product flow with 5 producers; the provider's ref_flow matches, it has no product inputs (hence no cut-offs and no self-consumption) and carries direct elementary outputs at plausible magnitudes; the alternative exists with the same ref_flow; the printed unit is m2 and 2.22 kg/m2 is a defensible light-mesh factor (my own range 2.2-3.0 kg/m2, the Korean phi6@150 fabric giving 2.96). map.why: The curators' hint flow 08a91e70-3ddc-11dd-9634-0050c2490048 'bentonite' is an ELEMENTARY flow (ELCD resource-from-ground), not a product flow. Its only genuine 'producer', 'Extraction ; Bentonite ; Raw bentonite ; Surface mining ; NESPS2' (8f381c93-9517-46d5-89eb-cd3cb582de28, CN 2019), emits that elementary flow as its reference output, which violates the repo's contract (reference/build_case_bundle.py --check reports 'not a product flow'; the matrix convention links foreground items to product flows). The second 'producer' 88ee466e is a data error (printing process with bentonite as a reference INPUT). The closest structurally valid dataset is the sibling NESPS2 record for soft clay: same source (2nd National Pollution Source Census coefficient handbook, code 1013 vs 1019 for bentonite), same scope (open-pit mining, gate-to-gate), same content (a single PM2.5-PM10 dust emission: 0.0625 kg/t vs 0.082 kg/t for bentonite), geo CN, year 2019, a Product-flow reference output with exactly one producer, and it does not consume its own reference flow. Bentonite is a montmorillonite soft clay that is surface-mined, so the physical proxy is reasonable. What it misrepresents: (1) generic clay, not sodium/calcium bentonite; (2) NESPS2 is a pollution-coefficient dataset, so there is no diesel, electricity, blasting, drying, milling or Na-activation, and no transport; (3) no mineral-resource extraction row; (4) in this snapshot the PM2.5-PM10 flow has no characterisation factor in any of the 25 LCIA methods, so bentonite will show up only as an inventory line and contribute exactly 0 to every impact score. This is numerically harmless for the case: literature cradle-to-gate bentonite is of order 0.02-0.03 kg CO2-eq/kg, i.e. roughly 5 kg CO2-eq for 211 kg, far below 0.01 % of the SVE system dominated by 148,748 kWh of electricity. Use it with confidence=low and say so in the teaching material; for a sensitivity exercise one could instead hand-build a 'bentonite, cradle-to-gate' column from the CEEIO 'Non-metallic minerals mining' sector (needs an uncertain kg-to-EUR price conversion and is self-consuming, so it is not listed as an alternative).

convert.note: Engineering assumption, not from the paper: SVE vapour lines are typically 2-3 inch (50-75 mm) flexible hose. A 50 mm bore TPU hose with ~3 mm wall at TPU density ~1.2 g/cm3 weighs pi*(0.028^2-0.025^2)*1200 = ~0.60 kg/m; catalogue weights for 2-3 inch PU suction/ducting hose span roughly 0.3-0.9 kg/m. 0.5 kg/m is a mid-range value (340 m -> 170 kg); treat as +/-50% and run 0.3-1.0 kg/m in sensitivity. corrected.convert_note: Engineering assumption, not from the paper (paper gives length only). SVE vapour lines are typically 2-3 inch (50-75 mm) flexible PU hose. Reviewer's independent estimate: 2 in (51 mm bore) wire-helix PU suction/ducting hose weighs ~0.25-0.35 kg/m for light-duty 0.6-1.0 mm wall, ~0.5-0.7 kg/m for medium/heavy-duty 1.5-3 mm wall, and 3 in heavy-duty ~1.0-1.3 kg/m (manufacturer weight tables for PU suction/ducting hose; geometric check pi*(0.0285^2-0.0255^2)*1200 kg/m3 = 0.61 kg/m at 3 mm wall, TPU density 1.1-1.25 g/cm3). 0.5 kg/m is a defensible mid value (340 m -> 170 kg); run 0.3-1.0 kg/m as sensitivity. TianGong's curators entered 340 kg (1:1 unit mismatch), i.e. the top of that band.
corrected.why: Verified: TianGong has no polyurethane polymer, TPU or PU-hose production process. The curators' hint flow 'Flexible Polyurethane Hose' (0d947db3) has zero producers (340 kg cut-off in KR process d58c1c06); 'Plastic pipes' (554160db) also has zero producers; every PU-related record (polyether polyol 060c8aec, PU foam 60670a4c, spandex MDI/PTMEG d6aa3fad, PU synthetic leather 131a20d5, plastic tube extrusion 7bd61ed6, rubber sheet/tube cfd8a022) is a NESPS2 census emission-factor sheet with only VOC/PM/COD outputs, no resin or energy inputs and no CO2, so linking to any of them would make the hose look impact-free for GWP. The hose is therefore represented by mass as a generic thermoplastic. HDPE production CN 2020 (d8dddfbb) is the best available generic polymer dataset: recent, Chinese, with direct fossil CO2 2.35 kg/kg and an electricity input (1.5 MJ/kg) and hydrogen input (0.11 kg/kg) that link to providers; its ref_flow equals the chosen flow and it does not consume PE-HD. PP 2020 (90cdb77a, 1.21 kg CO2/kg, 1.64 kg naphtha unlinked) is the only comparable generic polymer and is not better. Known misrepresentations: (1) PE instead of TPU, likely ~2x underestimate of embodied GWP; (2) hose extrusion omitted (only VOC/PM would change); (3) ethylene 1.02 kg/kg is an elementary input so cracking/refining is outside the boundary; (4) CO 1.76 and NOx 0.32 kg/kg look mis-scaled and may inflate POCP/acidification; (5) kg/m is assumed. The second PE-HD producer 5f2f416a (Donghai Bridge wind-farm PE, SH-CN 2009, 17.6 TJ geothermal energy per 257 t) is listed only because it is a valid provider of the same flow; it is a site-specific record, not a sensible generic proxy. issues: Propylene input (4f1a182b, 1.05 kg/kg PP) has 7 producers but one of them, 625bc731 'Acrylic acid ; ... NESPS2' (geo=CN, 2019), is a mislabelled emission-only record (VOC + exhaust gas, no inputs) whose ref_flow is propylene. The repo's automatic provider rule (same geo as consumer = 'CN', then most recent year) selects exactly this record over 0059b3c2 (CN 2010) and 08956b46 (CN 2002), because the real 2018 steam-cracking/MTO/PDH datasets carry sub-national geos (DL-LN-CN, ZJ-GD-CN, NJ-JS-CN). Unless propylene is pinned (e.g. d66440a7 steam cracking DL-LN-CN 2018, or 0059b3c2 CN 2010), the upstream cracker burden of PP silently drops to ~zero. The mapper's claim that the 7 producers all have 'their own elementary flows and electricity' is therefore overstated.

map.why: The curators' hint flow 'Tap Water' (e5fef5ef, kg) is verified: 8 producers, 53 consumers, all CN 2019 unit processes with ref_flow = this flow, so it links in the matrix. Chosen provider: conventional surface-water coagulation/sedimentation/filtration/disinfection train, the standard municipal treatment in Korea and China, so technology scope is right (mains water delivered to site for biopile moisture control). Among the eight NESPS2 tap-water datasets it is the only coagulation-train one that lists each pollutant once (one COD, one total-P, one organic-N, one NH3-N, one waste-water line), so summing exchanges into B does not double count; the mid (6b77b560) and large (d9efb042) plant datasets list the same pollutant 2-3 times (generation vs discharge coefficients under different end-of-pipe options, e.g. waste water 43.6 / 42.728 / 3.488 kg) and would be over-counted by a naive matrix build. What it misrepresents: every NESPS2 tap-water producer is a pollutant-discharge-coefficient dataset with OUTPUTS ONLY, no inputs at all, so there is no electricity for pumping/treatment (~0.2-0.4 kWh/m3 in reality), no coagulant/chlorine, and no 'freshwater' resource withdrawal from nature; the only impacts the chain carries are tiny COD/N/P water emissions per kg (e.g. 1.1e-6 kg COD/kg). convert.note: Stoichiometric ammonia content of ammonium sulphate. (NH4)2SO4 is made by neutralising ammonia with sulfuric acid: 2 NH3 + H2SO4 -> (NH4)2SO4. Every other nitrogen-chemical route in the snapshot (NESPS2 pollution-census datasets for synthetic ammonia x17, urea x11, ammonium nitrate x2, compound fertiliser x4, sulfuric acid x4) is a pollutant-only stub with zero product or energy inputs, so using one would record a few grams of PM and N-to-water and nothing of the ammonia synthesis that dominates the burden; the NESPS2 'Synthetic ammonia' reference flow 82980072 is not even present in the flow table.
